learningOutcomes: ADMISSION AND REPORTING
By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Identify and explain key ergonomics risk factors in ICT workspaces.
Demonstrate correct sitting posture and workstation setup.
Apply ergonomic practices while using computer systems.
traineeActivities: Adjust workstation based on trainer feedback.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Create document.
Format text.
Save the document with proper naming.
traineeActivities: Save the document in a folder.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Format paragraphs.
Set margins/orientation.
Insert breaks and headers.
By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Insert tables.
Format table elements.
Modify rows/columns.
By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a. Open/edit documents, use find/replace, track changes.
b. Explain mail merge, create recipient list, and merge data.
c. Insert images/shapes/charts, position objects, format.
trainerActivities: Provide documents, explain tools, and supervise editing.
Demonstrate process, provide example lists, and supervise.
Explain objects, show formatting tools, assign tasks
traineeActivities: Edit sample report, add comments, and track changes.
Create document, import recipients, merge and preview.
Insert and format different objects in document.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a. Insert captions, create list of figures, and update lists.
b. Use heading styles, generate table, and update fields.
c. Adjust print settings, preview documents, print.
trainerActivities: Demonstrate caption tool, guide practice, and explain updates.
Explain heading structure, demonstrate TOC tool, and give tasks.
Guide print process, explain settings, and check outputs.
traineeActivities: Caption images, generate and update list.
Apply styles, generate and update TOC.
Print sample documents with specific layout settings.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a) Open Excel, create workbook, and add/switch sheets.
b) Use relative/absolute referencing, apply in formulas.
c) Apply basic formula such as addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.
trainerActivities: Demonstrate workbook setup, assign workbook task.
Explain cell types, show examples, assign tasks.
Demonstrate formulas, explain errors, and assign exercise.
traineeActivities: Perform tasks using all reference types.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a)  Use SUM, AVERAGE, MAX, and MIN.
b) Format numbers, text, borders, alignment.
c) Combine spreadsheet skills, save/print workbook.
trainerActivities: Explain function syntax, assign data tasks.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a)  Select data; insert chart types, format charts.
b) Apply conditional logic and lookups.
c) Restrict entries protect sheets, set passwords.
trainerActivities: Demonstrate chart tools, assign data set.
Explain logic functions, provide data, and guide tasks.
traineeActivities: Apply data rules and protect sheets.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a)  Sort ranges, apply filters, and extract info.
b) Set print area, headers, orientation.
c) Create analytical workbook, include charts.

schedule.sessionTitle: Introduction to Computerized Databases and User Requirements
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a)  Define key database terms (table, record, and field).
b) Explain how databases are organized.
c) Identify what users need in a database.
trainerActivities:  Guide trainees in a user requirement activity.
traineeActivities:  Label parts of a sample database.
 Interview a classmate to gather user needs.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a)  Create a basic ERD (Entity Relationship Diagram).
b) Turn the ERD into a table structure.
c)  Identify keys (primary and foreign).
trainerActivities: Help trainees build a simple database design.
Draw ERDs from a case study.
traineeActivities:  Label keys in a sample database.

schedule.sessionTitle: Creating Tables, Forms, Queries, and Reports
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a)   Create tables with fields and records.
b)  Make forms and queries.
c)  Create basic reports.
trainerActivities: Demonstrate how to create database objects.
traineeActivities:  Build tables in a database software (e.g., MS Access).
 Create a report from database data.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
a)   Add, edit, and delete records.
b) Search and filter data.
c) Print tables, forms, and reports.
trainerActivities:  How to edit and print data.
 Give tasks to practice data manipulation.
traineeActivities:  Enter and update data in tables.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Identify types of presentation layouts.
Design and create PowerPoint slides.
Save a PowerPoint presentation.
trainerActivities:  Explain layout types and design tips.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Apply animations and transitions.
Insert text, tables, and charts.
Prepare and print a presentation.
trainerActivities:  Show how to apply animations and insert objects.
traineeActivities:  Insert a table or chart into a slide.

schedule.sessionTitle: Introduction to Graphic Design Tools and Requirements
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
 Define key terms in graphic design and identify types of graphic software.
 List various types of publication designs (e.g., flyers, posters, cards).
 Identify elements of a graphic application window.
trainerActivities: Explain basic graphic design terms and software types.
Show samples of different publication designs.
traineeActivities:  Explore types of designs (banners, brochures, certificates, etc.).
 Label parts of a graphic application window.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
 Create and format basic publication using graphic software.
 Add and edit content such as text, shapes, and pictures.
 Set up and print a graphic publication.
trainerActivities:  Demonstrate how to add and format content.
 Guide students in using tools like headers, watermarks, and page setup.
 Supervise print setup and printing process.
traineeActivities:  Create a sample publication (e.g., flyer or certificate).
 Perform print setup and print the final design.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Explain the basics of document production and identify types of printers and scanners.
Demonstrate how to print and scan a document.
Understand the process of document duplication.
trainerActivities:  Introduce key terms and concepts in document printing and scanning.
 Demonstrate how to operate printers and scanners.
 Guide learners in hands-on practice of printing, scanning, and duplicating documents.
traineeActivities:  Observe and identify different types of printers and scanners.
 Practice printing and scanning a sample document.
 Duplicate a scanned document using available tools.

learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Define online collaboration and explain its importance.
Identify various online collaboration tools (e.g., Zoom, Google Drive, Teams).
List key factors to consider when choosing a collaboration tool.
trainerActivities:  Explain key concepts and uses of online collaboration.
 Show examples of platforms like Google Meet, Skype, and Slack.
 Lead a class discussion and tool comparison.
traineeActivities:  Discuss the meaning and benefits of online collaboration.
 Explore and list common collaboration tools.
 Compare tools based on features, accessibility, and use.

schedule.sessionTitle: Setting Up and Using Online Collaboration Tools
learningOutcomes: By the end of the session, the learners should be able to:
Set up and register for online collaboration platforms.
Use tools like email, cloud storage, and calendars in collaboration.
Understand mobile collaboration and synchronization.
trainerActivities:  Guide trainees through downloading and installing tools.
 Demonstrate email functions and calendar sharing.
 Explain mobile collaboration and supervise practice.
traineeActivities:  Create user accounts and set up software (e.g., Google Drive, Teams).
 Send and organize emails; use shared calendars.
 Explore mobile collaboration features (e.g., app permissions, sync tools).
